# UNDERWRITING MEMORANDUM — GOLD.com, Inc. (NYSE: GOLD)

---

## SECTION 0 — OVERVIEW

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Ticker / Company | GOLD / Gold.com, Inc. — fully integrated precious-metals platform (wholesale dealer, DTC retailer, minter, vaulter, secured lender) |
| Price T0 | **$42.29** [live quote, 2026-10-02] |
| Market cap / shares | $1.232B / 27.26M diluted (filed FY2026 count; see Section 3) |
| **Verdict** | **UNDERVALUED** (value basis; crux on growth_years_3_5 — see Section 3) |
| Base IV | **$55.72** (+31.8% MoS) |
| Bull IV | **$138.53** (+227.6%) |
| Bear IV | **$28.38** (−32.9%) |
| Probability-weighted expected IV | $69.59 (+64.6% vs T0) |
| Action | **Accumulate**, 3.0% capped ledger weight, staged tranches ($42.29 starter / $28.38 core) |

The price is paying ~$42 for a business whose owner cash flow the market's own structure implies shrinking ~15–18%/yr for five years — i.e., pricing Gold.com as if it were *only* the 1.8%-margin gold pass-through that is bleeding revenue as gold corrects 25% from its January 2026 high. The filings and dated third-party evidence show a second engine — secured metals leases (a $1.7B book in which Tether is the dominant creditor), storage, secured lending ($25.6M FY26 interest income) and minting/logistics services (Costco vendor; SMI sovereign-mint capacity) — that does not scale down with the gold price. That is the disagreement with the price, stated precisely in Section 3.

---

## SECTION 1 — MACRO (DATA 1.5 / 1.6)

- **Rates:** 10y nominal 5.24%, real 2.88%, breakeven 2.36%; curve +0.45% and steepening; IG spread 1.49%, HY OAS 3.24%. News of 2026-09-25 reports markets pricing *possible additional hikes* against sticky inflation (CPI 3.35%, PCE 3.42%).
- **Active shock:** `oil_shock` (severity 1, up, onset 2026-09-28) with the Strait of Hormuz closure unresolved (2026-09-26, 2026-10-04 items) — an energy-price spike that keeps inflation persistent and gold's structural bid (central-bank/investor accumulation) intact.
- **Regime:** goldilocks 0.341 headline but contested (margin 0.070); tightening 0.176 is the live risk.
- **Transmission to GOLD (four channels):**
  1. *Gold price → pass-through revenue.* Gold corrected from the January 2026 ATH of **$5,608.35** (TradingEconomics, verified) to **~$4,184/oz on 2026-09-30** (fetched quote page). Notional revenue falls ~1:1 with the price: consensus models current-FY revenue −15.9% and next-FY −12.9% [Estimate, DATA 8].
  2. *Inflation persistence → fee engine.* The same macro that hurts the top line (Hormuz, Ukraine, Iran escalation per DATA 1.6) is what drives sovereign/investor gold accumulation — the demand behind storage, vaulting and lease fees.
  3. *Higher rates → discount rate + consumer demand.* COE anchor 8.98%; DTC discretionary demand (TV/radio/digital retail) is rate-sensitive — Q4 FY26 DTC new customers fell to 67.9K from 108.9K YoY [Actual, PRIMARY P1].
  4. *Stablecoin liquidity → funding engine.* The Tether lease relationship is a crypto-issuer credit line in disguise; a tightening regime that stresses stablecoin liquidity is the single most important Bear transmission (Section 4).

---

## SECTION 2 — BUSINESS & MOAT

**Economic engines (Pillar 1 deconstruction):**

| Engine | FY2026 evidence | Character |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Transactional pass-through** — Wholesale $19.4B net of eliminations (GM 0.72%) + DTC $6.1B (GM 5.14%) [Actual, PRIMARY P2] | Consolidated GM 1.78%; revenue scales with gold price × ounces (FY26: 2.03M oz gold sold) | Cyclical notional flow; ~98% of revenue; no pricing power on the metal |
| **B. Captive/recurring fee base** — Secured metals leases ($1.7B book, Tether dominant creditor [Estimate, Bloomberg 2026-09-16]); secured lending (367 loans, $115.1M receivable at 6/30/26; FY26 interest income $25.6M) [Actual, PRIMARY P1/P2]; storage ("continued growth in our storage and secured lending businesses… attractive economics" [Actual, PRIMARY P1]); CyberMetals digital custody AUM $16.6M [Actual, PRIMARY P1]; Costco vendor contract for minting/logistics/trading via Silver Gold Bull Calgary [Estimate, fetched Yahoo 2026-09-13] | Fee revenue decoupled from gold price; the lease book is *revolving*, not multi-year contracted backlog — no cite-able backlog floor exists in the pack's filings, so no Bear floor applies (charter mandate 4) |
| **C. Strategic optionality** — SMI minting capacity "well positioned to serve the growing demand from the United States Mint and other sovereign mints" [Actual, PRIMARY P1]; tokenized-gold distribution via Tether; digital/social retail platforms for younger buyers [Estimate, fetched Yahoo]; Atkinsons 49.5% stake [Unconfirmed] | Early-stage; credited only qualitatively in Bull |

**Owner earnings (mandate 2):** FY2026 owner earnings **$103M** after SBC [Actual, DATA 3; SBC $2M already expensed in net income — counted once via `sbc_treatment: deducted_in_cf`]. Non-GAAP EBITDA $179.8M [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. The FY26 OCF of $1.22B is **not** recurring owner cash flow: it embeds trading/lease working-capital float (current liabilities $3.15B vs current assets $3.60B; inventory up to $1.56B) [Actual, DATA 6A]. The desk's WC treatment deducts only the growth-linked WC (2.9% of revenue change); in a falling-revenue path that term is *negative* (cash release), which is why Base year-1 CF prints above the $103M base.

**Moat (7 factors, 0–3 each):** Brand portfolio (JM Bullion, Stack's BGA, Monex, SMI) **2**; Distribution breadth (TV/radio/digital + Costco + sovereign mints) **2**; Switching costs (DTC low; storage/lease relationships sticky) **1**; Scale/cost advantage (integrated minting–logistics–trading at top-2 US dealer scale) **2**; Network effects **0**; Pricing power (1.8% GM pass-through; fee streams modest) **1**; Regulatory/licensing barriers (minting, sovereign contracts, vaulting) **2**. **Total 10/21 → 2.9 / 5.0**, direction *improving but fragile* — scale is real, durability is unproven at these margins.

**Financial strength: weak-to-moderate.** Net cash +$485M on the pack's card [Actual, DATA 6], but equity is only $876M against $4.1B of assets, and current liabilities include ~$1.45B owed to Tether in payables/advances at 6/30/26 [Unconfirmed — Bloomberg/cryptobriefing citing the 10-K; note not in pack]. The CIBC facility was converted on 2026-09-29 into an **uncommitted, on-demand $250M** revolver (cut from $427.5M) [Actual, PRIMARY P3]. Liquidity is therefore: Tether's willingness to roll + the ability to shrink inventory. That is a real tail, priced into Bear.

---

## SECTION 3 — VALUATION (desk inputs, departures, terminal, reverse DCF, crux)

| Input | Value | Default? | Departure reason (dated evidence) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frame / rate | Equity frame; COE **8.98%** | = anchor | Flows are after interest (DATA 5); no adjustment |
| base_cf (Base) | **$103M** FY2026 owner earnings | = default | None needed |
| Base explicit CF growth y1–y5 | −4.9% / +31.6% / **−10% / −8% / −6%** | y1–2 = consensus EPS levels (default); y3–5 above next-FY revenue growth (−12.9%) | `guidance_deviation_reason`: notional top line falls with gold (spot $4,184 on 2026-09-30 vs ATH $5,608.35 in Jan 2026, TradingEconomics) while the fee engine grows — Tether accounted for the majority of the $1.7B lease book (Bloomberg, 2026-09-16), storage/lease fees and $25.6M interest income [Actual, PRIMARY P2] do not shrink with the metal price; CF therefore declines materially less than revenue |
| Bull y2 / y3–5 | +104.1% (to consensus-high level $200M) / +12% / +10% / +8% | y2 = bull2 default level | Gold re-acceleration or lease-book scaling to multiples of initial figures [Estimate, fetched Yahoo 2026-09-13]; SMI sovereign-mint share gains [Actual, PRIMARY P1] |
| Bear y2 / y3–5; wacc | −49% (to $50M) / −10% / −5% / 0%; **10.48%** (+150bp) | y2 is 36% below bear2 ($78M) | `scenario_deviation_reason`: consensus does not model Tether counterparty stress — ~$1.45B owed to one crypto issuer [Unconfirmed, Bloomberg 2026-09-16] with the only bank line uncommitted/on-demand (PRIMARY P3, 2026-09-29); a non-roll forces lease unwinds and collateral calls exactly as gold sits −25% from ATH; +150bp credit-spread shock per mandate 4 |
| fade_years | 5 | = default | Fee-engine runway (lease book, Costco, SMI) justifies 5y before convergence |
| terminal_g / terminal_ronic | **3.75% / 54.33%** | = defaults | No departure; ronic is the 8-year record median return on tangible capital (p=1.0 above COE) |
| Shares | **27,262,600** | ≠ default 29,154,756 | `shares_reason`: FY2026 filed diluted EPS $3.02 on $82.3M NI (PRIMARY P1, 2026-09-03) implies ~27.25M diluted shares, matching the filed weighted-average count (DATA 6B); the vendor count is flagged stale in the pack itself |
| Cash-flow life | Perpetual | — | No depleting reserves or expiring licence; FY26 capex $13M vs $25.5B revenue [Actual, DATA 5] is maintenance-level; gold price deck: flows assume spot stabilizing $3,800–4,500 (Base), re-accelerating (Bull), −25%+ further (Bear) |

**Terminal & cross-check:** Base terminal = Gordon at 3.75% on funded earnings with ronic fading from 54.3%; **implied terminal EV/FCF multiple 19.84x** vs the MRI financials sector band (median 11.73x, p75 17.88x) and cluster peer median 17.4x → **+2.4x above the cluster median**. Reconciliation: the multiple is mechanical output of COE 8.98% / g 3.75% / ronic 54.3% — a trading-and-fee platform whose new-investment returns (lease fees on posted collateral, minting services) are far above bank-like financials; but the terminal is **38% of Base value**, so if long-run ronic compresses toward COE the multiple collapses toward ~1/(r−g) territory. This is the single most sensitive construction in the model and the main reason the weight is capped at 3%.

**Reverse DCF (mandate 3b):** Under the neutral reference structure the price implies solved initial growth of **−10.8%** and a **10-year CAGR of −2.9%** — *below* the base-rate median (4.3%) for the $10–50B bucket (p50 4.3%, p90 14.0%); under my own structure the implied stage-1 growth is **−7.5%/yr**. The market is pricing a structurally *shrinking* cash flow — below even the base-rate median for a company that grew revenue +27.4% CAGR over the last five years [Actual, DATA 7].

**price_implied (my inputs):** coe 11.80% (mine 8.98%) · growth_years_3_5 **−17.8%/yr** (mine −8.0%/yr) · year2_level $0.088B (mine $0.129B) · fade / terminal_g / terminal_ronic: not reachable inside bounds.

**CRUX — growth_years_3_5:** my value **−8.0%/yr** vs price-implied **−17.8%/yr**, a ~9.8pp gap. The price says owner CF falls nearly as fast as notional revenue through year 5, i.e., the fee engine adds nothing while gold corrects. Dated evidence to the contrary: (i) storage and secured lending "carry attractive economics" and grew through the year [Actual, PRIMARY P1, 2026-09-03]; (ii) SMI "significantly expands our total production capacity… clear pathway to capturing additional value and market share globally" [Actual, PRIMARY P1]; (iii) the Tether partnership "has scaled past what was originally disclosed at launch, with lease positions and storage volumes now at multiples of the initial figures," plus Costco minting/logistics/trading services [Estimate, fetched Yahoo article, 2026-09-13]. A business whose CF fell 17.8%/yr would not be growing a $1.7B secured-lease book and adding a sovereign-mint capacity pathway in the same year.

---

## SECTION 4 — SCENARIOS (last complete desk run, exact values)

| Scenario | p | IV/share | vs T0 | Causal path |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## SECTION 7 — RISKS & PRE-MORTEM

**Main risks:**
1. **Tether concentration (the big one):** ~$1.45B of payables/advances to one stablecoin issuer [Unconfirmed]; a regulatory action, stablecoin outflow event or simple non-roll unwinds the volume engine overnight.
2. **Gold price continuation:** another 20–30% decline compresses pass-through revenue, inventory values and lease-collateral headroom simultaneously; DTC demand is already soft (new customers −38% YoY in Q4 [Actual, PRIMARY P1]).
3. **Integration/SG&A:** SG&A +46% in FY26 [Actual, DATA 5] against a shrinking top line is negative operating leverage until fee revenue catches up; CFO and auditor transitions add friction.
4. **Funding structure:** uncommitted, on-demand $250M bank line (PRIMARY P3) means there is no committed backstop; the special dividend ($1.00/share) further draws cash.
5. **Data/coverage risk:** 3–4 analysts, 16.5% short interest [Aggregator, DATA 9]; vendor share count stale; Tether note not in pack.

**Pre-mortem — "we lost 50% of the capital in five years: what went wrong?"** A stablecoin-liquidity stress event forced Tether to demand settlement of its ~$1.45B position during a further gold decline; Gold.com had to sell inventory at a loss and shrink the lease book, fee revenue collapsed with it, SG&A fixed costs drove quarterly losses, the uncommitted CIBC line was unavailable when needed, and the market re-rated the equity from "fee platform" back to "levered metals trader" — landing at the Bear value ($28.38) and then below it as dilutive issuances (net_issuance > 0) funded the hole. The uncommitted line and the single counterparty were the two facts that made this path survivable-but-destructive rather than impossible.

## SECTION 9 — RED TEAM

**Strongest short thesis:** "GOLD is a ~2%-gross-margin notional pass-through whose record revenue is an artifact of buying dealers into a rising gold market. It owes ~$1.45B to a crypto issuer it cannot verify, its only bank line is uncommitted and on-demand, its CFO just retired, its auditor just changed, and the metal is down 25% from its high. The 'fee engine' is a revolving lease book one counterparty decision away from zero. At $42 you are paying ~13x a volatile earnings base for a balance sheet that depends on Tether's goodwill."

**My answer:** Conceded in full on the concentration — which is exactly why Bear is −33%, the weight is capped at 3%, and the first tranche is a starter, not a core. But three facts break the "worthless pass-through" framing: (i) the leases are *secured by posted gold* — Tether's credit is collateralized, and Tether holds a 12–13% equity stake [Unconfirmed], so a non-roll is costly to it too; (ii) the fee base is not only the lease book — $25.6M of FY26 interest income, storage growth, Costco services and SMI minting capacity are in filed releases [Actual, PRIMARY P1]; (iii) on paper the company is net cash +$485M [Actual, DATA 6] and can shrink inventory to release cash (FY26 WC already released $172M [Actual, DATA 6A]). The short thesis is a *tail*, not the modal outcome — hence 25% Bear probability, not more.
